resources.string: Get started by connecting\nyour devices to the TV
Pick “%1$s” in Screen Mirroring, not “%2$s”: that one is the TV’s own AirPlay, and it mirrors at 1080p.
Start Screen Mirroring on it to show its screen here.
Mirroring %1$s · press Back twice to stop
Press Back again to stop mirroring
%1$d × %2$d %3$s · %4$.0f fps · %5$.1f Mbit/s\ndecode %6$.1f ms · dropped %7$d · restarts %8$d\nTV offers %9$d × %10$d · pacing: %11$s
What Macs and iPhones show in Screen Mirroring

Macs, iPhones and iPads fit their screen inside this size, keeping its shape, exactly as picked. Auto (the default) is the sharpest this TV decodes: 4K when it can, so an upright iPhone sends about 1000 × 2160, every row the TV has. Show stats shows what arrives.
The most frames per second Macs and iPhones may send. 120 needs a 120 Hz TV screen, and Apple devices decide what they actually send: turn on Show stats to see it.
Shows each frame right away, one per screen refresh. Best for most networks.
Lowest delay. Motion can stutter if Wi-Fi delivers frames unevenly.
Holds one frame (about 17 ms) to smooth out a busy Wi-Fi network.

iPhones are wider than a TV. Fill zooms in to cover the TV and cuts off the left and right edges (a 16:9 video then fills it exactly); Fit shows the whole picture with black bars above and below; Stretch pulls it out to the whole screen, with nothing cut off and no bars, but everything a little wider. Mac screens and upright iPhones are never changed. While mirroring, press Up or Down to switch.
Black bars? Press Up to fill the screen
Filling the screen (sides cut off). Up to stretch, Down for the whole picture.
Whole picture. Up to fill the screen.
Stretched to the screen. Down to fill it without stretching.
Play the mirrored device’s sound on the TV
You can also press OK on the remote while mirroring
Stay visible after closing the app
Keeps the TV in Screen Mirroring lists while you use other apps
What the TV detected and offers, plus the recent AirPlay log. Useful when reporting a problem.
Allow the player to open by itself?
Visible, but Android won’t let the player open by itself while another app is on screen. Run this once from your Mac: %1$s

To start mirroring while another app is open, Android needs Mango Screen Cast For macOS/iOS to have “Display over other apps” permission. If this TV has no settings screen for it, run this once from your Mac:\n\n%1$s
Mango Screen Cast For macOS/iOS %1$s. Built on UxPlay (GPL-3.0), libplist (LGPL-2.1) and OpenSSL; set in Geist (SIL OFL). AirPlay is a trademark of Apple Inc.
To update itself, the app needs “Install unknown apps” allowed
Installing update… the app restarts by itself

Automatic installs new versions as soon as nothing is mirroring: the TV looks whenever this app comes up or mirroring ends, and every 10 minutes while the home screen is up. Ask first shows an Update button on the home screen.
Current version. New versions come from the project’s GitHub releases.
“%1$s” is visible to Macs, iPhones and iPads
